- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending up.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days) are common; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show high volatility or sharp moves, forecast should trend toward historical mean (last 10–15 days average) within 5–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; reduce first 3–5 forecast points by 1–3% to align with observed lag.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.67, -0.67, +0.67), model should smooth transitions; avoid abrupt directional shifts unless confirmed by price action.
